flatten.py:
"""Flatten arbitrarily nested lists."""


def flatten(items):
    """Return a new list with nested lists recursively flattened, in order.

    Only list instances are expanded; tuples, strings, dicts, sets and other
    objects are kept as single items. The input is never mutated. Uses an
    explicit stack, so deep nesting does not hit the recursion limit.
    A self-referencing list raises ValueError instead of looping forever.
    """
    result = []
    stack = [iter(items)]
    active = [id(items)]
    while stack:
        for item in stack[-1]:
            if isinstance(item, list):
                if id(item) in active:
                    raise ValueError("cannot flatten a self-referencing list")
                stack.append(iter(item))
                active.append(id(item))
                break
            result.append(item)
        else:
            stack.pop()
            active.pop()
    return result
